v3_detautology_of_record.interpretation: retention vs non-insider-HHI correlates -> de-tautology 'survives' in v3

v4_reviewed_detautology.reason: A valid v4 de-tautology requires v3's exact non_insider_hhi_approx methodology. Verification showed v3 non_insider_hhi_approx != full_hhi - insider_hhi_contribution (max abs err 0.145 over N=34), so the naive reconstruction (full_hhi - sum(v4_insider_share^2)) is the WRONG formula and its rho is invalid. An earlier in-cycle computation under that wrong formula returned rho=0.128 and is DISCARDED.
v4_reviewed_detautology.follow_on: Recompute non_insider_hhi under v3's actual definition (locate the v3-generation script in analysis/) with v4 insider flags, then re-test rho(v4_frac, non_insider_hhi_v4). Out of this cycle's reliable scope.

headline_note: The de-tautology is a robustness check on the insider-RETENTION measure, not the headline. The headline (DePIN sector concentration) is robust under all four retention vectors (b2_nansen_v4_headline_impact_results), and the retention regressor is n.s. throughout (channel-shift). The v4 de-tautology is a follow-on, not a blocker.
